paper_metadata.title: A Quantum Circuit Design for Quantum Portfolio Optimization Problem

experiments.description: Hybrid QPO/VQE portfolio optimization experiment on real cryptocurrency data, evaluating the VQE optimization branch of the proposed circuit against classical target portfolios over varying portfolio sizes.

algorithm.variant: QPO circuit operating in VQE mode

problem_formulation.encoding_details: n = log2(N) qubits encode the portfolio state |x̂⟩; in QPO mode the circuit uses n qubits for |x̂⟩ and n qubits for |μ̂⟩, with total 2n+2 qubits including control and ancilla when MCSWAP-TEST is enabled.
problem_formulation.objective_function: L(x) = q x^T Σ x - μ^T x, with discrete binary portfolio x and budget constraint b^T x <= B; QUBO form adds penalty P = λ(1^T x - B)^2.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Penalty term λ(1^T x - B)^2 for QUBO formulation; budget set as B = floor(|x_Xk|/2) in experiments.
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: Ising Hamiltonian of the form sum_{i,j} J_ij z_i z_j + sum_i h_i z_i + C after mapping x_i in {0,1} to z_i in {-1,1}.

problem_instance.description: Discrete portfolio optimization on subsets of cryptocurrency assets from Binance data, comparing predicted portfolios to linear-programming target portfolios.
problem_instance.num_assets: 2 to 16 per evaluated subset; source pool contains 97 assets

dataset_specification.preprocessing: Daily open and close prices used to compute per-asset return as (close - open) / open; average return over the two-month period used as mean return.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Compute mean returns and covariance matrix from daily price data; prepare encoded quantum states using qo|op package.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compute Hamming distance between predicted and target portfolios; compare against classical linear-programming solution.

speedup_claims.factor: O(log N) vs O(N^2) / O(N^3) / O(2^N)
speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical portfolio optimization methods (brute-force search, linear programming, mean-variance optimization)
speedup_claims.conditions: for very large portfolios / millions of assets in the hybrid quantum-classical setting
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a complexity claim in the introduction; the paper does not empirically demonstrate asymptotic speedup on large-scale hardware.

experiments.description: Hybrid QPO/MCSWAP-TEST experiment measuring the return-value overlap term <mu-hat|x-hat> within the proposed circuit on the same cryptocurrency portfolio instances.

algorithm.variant: QPO circuit with MCSWAP-TEST sub-circuit enabled

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Prepare |x̂⟩ and |μ̂⟩ using n = log2(N) qubits each; MCSWAP-TEST uses two control Hadamards and n multi-control SWAP gates acting on wires (0,1,2,2+n), ..., (0,1,1+n,1+2n).
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate return value as |x||μ| <μ̂|x̂> from measurement probabilities P(0) and P(1), where <μ̂|x̂> = sqrt(P(0) - P(1)).
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Same QUBO penalty formulation as the VQE branch; MCSWAP-TEST is activated by control qubit k = 1.

problem_instance.description: Same real cryptocurrency portfolio instances as the QPO VQE experiment; evaluates overlap/return estimation on subsets of assets.
problem_instance.num_assets: 2 to 16 per evaluated subset; source pool contains 97 assets

dataset_specification.preprocessing: Daily open/close returns averaged over two months; normalized vectors x̂ and μ̂ used for overlap estimation.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Prepare normalized states and run MCSWAP-TEST; compute exact and estimated overlap values.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compute mean square error (MSE) between exact and estimated <μ̂|x̂>; acceptance threshold reported as 10^-2.

speedup_claims.caveats: The MCSWAP-TEST sub-circuit is presented as a functional extension for overlap estimation, not as a speedup benchmark.

experiments.description: QAOA baseline experiment on the same discrete portfolio optimization instances, used for comparison with VQE/QPO across portfolio sizes.

algorithm.parameter_initialization: Initialize qubits in superposition using Hadamard gates

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Binary portfolio variables x_i in {0,1} mapped to Ising variables z_i in {-1,1}; QAOA applied to the resulting Hamiltonian.
problem_formulation.objective_function: min_x [q x^T Σ x - μ^T x + λ(1^T x - B)^2]
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: Ising Hamiltonian derived from QUBO; coefficients J_ij and h_i.

problem_instance.description: Discrete portfolio optimization on subsets of cryptocurrency assets from Binance data.
problem_instance.num_assets: 2 to 16 per evaluated subset; source pool contains 97 assets

dataset_specification.preprocessing: Daily open and close prices used to compute average returns over two months.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Compute mean returns and covariance matrix; construct QUBO/Ising formulation.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compare predicted portfolios to target portfolios using Hamming distance.

speedup_claims.factor: O(log N) qubits for hybrid quantum-classical processing
speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical methods with polynomial or exponential scaling
speedup_claims.conditions: for processing N assets in the hybrid quantum-classical approach
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper states the qubit count scales as n = log2(N), but does not provide a measured runtime speedup on hardware.
